questions.question: Which test is most likely to break when you improve the code without changing behaviour?
options: A test that the result's status is needs_review
A test that the store is empty after weak evidence
A test that about_page was called before suggest
A test that confidence is between 0 and 1
questions.explanation: Call order is an internal step. The other three check what callers can observe, which a refactoring keeps the same.

questions.question: Why does the fixture use a fixed clock?
options: So checked_at is the same on every run and can be asserted
questions.explanation: A real clock gives a different time on every run. Injecting a fixed time makes the test deterministic.

questions.question: What does the property test find that example tests usually miss?
options: Inputs nobody thought to write down, such as empty text
questions.explanation: Generated inputs explore cases beyond the hand-picked examples, such as text with no words at all.
